raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3 normalizes and rotates q/k with `fused_qknorm_rope_warp`. With head_dim 128 the kernel gives each warp one (token, head) row, so a lane moves only 8 bytes per row. The kernel is issue-bound, not bandwidth-bound: ncu shows 0.69 IPC per scheduler with 48% of stalls on L1TEX, and it reaches 2.5 TB/s on H200. It runs on every block: in place on the sequential Ulysses path, and once per head group and destination on the pipelined path (#43164).

## Modifications

- `fused_qknorm_rope_half_warp`: the same kernel with two rows per warp. Each row gets 16 lanes, and each lane moves 16 B of q/k and 16 B of the cos/sin cache.
- **Bit-identical by construction.** Each lane covers two lanes of the warp kernel. It keeps their two partial sums, accumulated in the same order, and replays that kernel's xor butterfly:
  - offsets 16..2 become 8..1, applied to each partial;
  - the final xor-1 step becomes `part0 + part1`.

  The per-element norm and RoPE expressions are unchanged.
- It is chosen at compile time for head_dim 128, NeoX, the norm rounded before RoPE, a half-width cache, and CUDA. Every other instantiation keeps the warp kernel.
- `_jit_qknorm_rope_module(half_warp=False)` keeps the warp kernel for the new test.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_qknorm_rope_out_of_place.py::test_two_rows_per_warp_match_one_row_per_warp` (new) compares the two kernels' bytes. It covers:
  - in-place and out-of-place;
  - BF16 and FP16 activations, with BF16, FP16 and FP32 caches;
  - rope_dim 32, 96 and 128;
  - int32 and int64 positions;
  - an odd row count, so the last warp gets one row.

  The file is now registered on `1-gpu-large` as well as `4-gpu-b200`, so both Hopper and Blackwell check the claim.
- `test_rope.py` passes all 1264 cases on H200, including the `torch.equal` checks against the split QK-norm + `sgl_kernel` RoPE baseline at H3's shape.
- Old and new outputs are byte-identical at H3's per-rank shapes (24826 / 18871 / 9436 tokens, in place and per exchange block).
- End to end on 4×H200, the MP4 md5 is unchanged in every arm: Ref2VA at Ulysses 2 (four runs), and T2VA at Ulysses 2 and 4.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per call on H200 (the same GPU for every column), 56 + 56 heads in place, or one exchange block on the pipelined path:

| tokens | path | before | after |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 24826 | in place, 56 + 56 heads | 567.5 µs (2.5 TB/s) | 430.5 µs (3.3 TB/s), −24% |
| 24826 | exchange block, 4 + 4 heads | 51.9 µs | 40.5 µs, −22% |
| 18871 | in place | 430.0 µs | 329.1 µs, −23% |
| 18871 | exchange block, 4 + 4 heads | 40.5 µs | 32.5 µs, −20% |
| 9436 | in place | 218.6 µs | 170.0 µs, −22% |
| 9436 | exchange block, 2 + 2 heads | 15.0 µs | 13.0 µs, −13% |

Two rows per warp with scalar cos/sin loads already gave 440.6 / 45.4 µs at 24826 tokens. The 16 B cache loads add the rest.

End to end, client latency, 4×H200, 50 steps, default quality. These runs sit on top of #43164 and #43327, and the arms differ only by this PR:

| Case | before | after | e2e | denoise stage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ref2VA 5 s, Ulysses 2 (ABBA) | 218.71 / 218.97 s | 218.47 / 218.70 s | −0.12% | 212.49 → 212.24 s |
| T2VA 5 s, Ulysses 2 | 140.76 s | 140.30 s | −0.33% | 137.01 → 136.55 s |
| T2VA 5 s, Ulysses 4 | 71.83 s | 71.68 s | −0.20% | 70.03 → 69.86 s |

On the pipelined path the kernel runs once per head group and destination, interleaved with attention. The H200s sit at their 700 W cap during denoise, so part of the freed time comes back as a lower clock.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -41,6 +41,9 @@ class CaseSpec:
     # Z-Image-Turbo default 1024x1024 config: dim=3840, num_heads=30 -> head_dim=128.
     CaseSpec("zimage_1024", 1, 4096, 30, 128, 128, False),
     CaseSpec("longcat_1024", 1, 4608, 24, 128, 128, False, True, True),
+    # MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA at Ulysses 2: 24826 tokens per rank, NeoX over the first
+    # 96 of 128 dims, norm rounded before RoPE (the two-rows-per-warp kernel).
+    CaseSpec("minimax_h3_ref2va", 1, 24826, 56, 128, 96, True, False, True),
     CaseSpec("batch2_medium", 2, 2048, 24, 128, 128, False),
 )
 CASE_BY_NAME = {case.name: case for case in BENCH_CASES}

@@ -10,7 +10,8 @@
 )
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
 
-register_cuda_ci(est_time=20, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
 
 
 def test_out_of_place_qknorm_rope_matches_inplace_and_keeps_inputs() -> None:
@@ -44,5 +45,68 @@ def test_out_of_place_qknorm_rope_matches_inplace_and_keeps_inputs() -> None:
     assert torch.equal(q_out, q_ref) and torch.equal(k_out, k_ref)
 
 
+# each case JIT-builds two modules, so these cover the branches, not the product:
+# H3's own config both ways, then the FP32-cache, FP16, int32 and rope-width paths
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "out_of_place,rope_dim,dtype,cache_dtype,pos_dtype",
+    [
+        (False, 96, torch.bfloat16, torch.bfloat16, torch.int64),
+        (True, 96, torch.bfloat16, torch.bfloat16, torch.int64),
+        (True, 32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.int32),
+        (False, 128, torch.float16, torch.float16, torch.int32),
+    ],
+)
+def test_two_rows_per_warp_match_one_row_per_warp(
+    out_of_place: bool,
+    rope_dim: int,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    cache_dtype: torch.dtype,
+    pos_dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> None:
+    """head_dim 128 with the norm rounded before NeoX RoPE runs two rows per
+    warp; its bytes must equal the one-row-per-warp kernel's on every arch."""
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.rope.qknorm_rope_jit import (
+        _jit_qknorm_rope_module,
+    )
+
+    T, H, D = 1037, 7, 128  # an odd row count leaves the last warp one row
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(rope_dim)
+    qkv = (3 * torch.randn(T, 3 * H * D, generator=g)).to("cuda", dtype)
+    q = qkv[:, : H * D].view(T, H, D)
+    k = qkv[:, H * D : 2 * H * D].view(T, H, D)
+    qw = (torch.rand(D, generator=g) + 0.5).to("cuda", dtype)
+    kw = (torch.rand(D, generator=g) + 0.5).to("cuda", dtype)
+    freqs = 50 * torch.randn(T, rope_dim // 2, generator=g)
+    cache = torch.cat((freqs.cos(), freqs.sin()), -1).to("cuda", cache_dtype)
+    pos = torch.randperm(T, generator=g).to("cuda", pos_dtype)
+    outputs = []
+    for half_warp in (False, True):
+        module = _jit_qknorm_rope_module(
+            D,
+            rope_dim,
+            True,
+            dtype,
+            cache_dtype,
+            True,
+            False,
+            False,
+            out_of_place,
+            half_warp=half_warp,
+        )
+        if out_of_place:
+            q_out = torch.empty(T, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+            k_out = torch.empty_like(q_out)
+            module.qknorm_rope_out_of_place(
+                q, k, q_out, k_out, qw, kw, cache, pos, 1e-5
+            )
+            outputs.append((q_out, k_out))
+        else:
+            q2, k2 = q.clone(), k.clone()
+            module.qknorm_rope(q2, k2, qw, kw, cache, pos, 1e-5)
+            outputs.append((q2, k2))
+    (q_ref, k_ref), (q_new, k_new) = outputs
+    assert torch.equal(q_ref, q_new) and torch.equal(k_ref, k_new)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
